outcomeTags.tag: `required`: the expected outcome follows from the cited clauses and can fail an implementation. `labChoice`: the laboratory's outcome where the text leaves it open; a differing implementation is reported and does not fail.
outcomeTags.classTag: On a refusal, the verdict is compared under `tag`; the refusal class is compared only when `classTag` is `required` (the default). The laboratory refusal classes are `format`, `structure`, `integrity`, `signature`, `decode`, `root-pk-mismatch` and `delegation-invalid`; ENV names `integrity`, `signature` and `decode` refusals, and KEYS §2.7 names the last two. `detail` is the laboratory's label and is never compared for an implementation.

generator.deterministic: Fixed public test roots, frozen random values and RFC 6979 low-S ES256 nonces; `node generate.mjs --check` reproduces both files byte for byte.

decisions.text: Every value is computed under the laboratory deployment profile `tpnil-sdx-lab:v1` (fixtures/sdx/v1/deployment-profile.json). `proto` and the outer protected-header `proto` carry its format identifier `tpnil-sdx-lab:v1`. The signing key identifier is derived under [2, `sdx sign`] and the recipient identifiers under [2, `sdx encrypt`], with key ID `account/<accountId>/runtime/<runtimeId>/action/<actionId>` and, per field, `/field/<fieldName>` appended; the level-3 keyword `action` is the profile's reading R1. Basis: ENV §2, §2.1, §8.5, §8.6; KEYS §1.3.1, §1.6.1, §1.8.

Each case is a request of the laboratory driver contract (programs/proposals/sdx-data-sharing/0.1.0/driver-contract.md) and its expected result. A `read` case expects a projection: the tier reached, the verdict, the refusal class, `aid`, the header values, one entry per declared field in declared order with its state (`value`, `unset` or `redacted`) and the verifying signature's `kid` and shape. A `write` case expects either a writer refusal or an envelope; for an envelope the laboratory publishes its own bytes and the checks of `checkWrite` in src/sdx/env.mjs, and the read cases marked `fromWrite` are rerun on the writer's envelope.

Each signature is ES256 over UTF-8 of protectedB64 "." base64url(signedBytes), where signedBytes is the deterministic encoding of {hdr, au, pr} and the protected header is the JSON {"alg":"ES256","kid":<kid>}; `sigs` carries `payload` "" and the 64-byte P1363 signature. A reader verifies over the carried protected value, so a protected header serialised in another member order verifies (`labChoice`). Basis: ENV §8.2, §8.3, §16.

The superseded candidate re-encodes the decoded {hdr, au, pr} with every integer that needs the 8-byte head (at least 2^32, or below -2^32) written as binary64; `tm` is such an integer on every record. Candidates are rebuilt from decoded values, so an audit layer carried in the superseded shape still verifies on the first candidate when its signature covers the current shape. A signature over any other encoding is refused. The projection reports the shape that verified. Basis: ENV §3 rule 2, §8.3; VEC `historical-float64-decode`.

A root record's `kid` is the hex of the per-record signing key the writer derives from its own root under the signing protocol identifier and the record key path, counterparty itself, and `hdr.pk` is that key. Any reader checks that a verifying signature names `hdr.pk`; only a root-holder can re-derive the expected key, and a mismatch is `root-pk-mismatch`. A reader that does not hold the root accepts a record whose key is not the derived one. Basis: ENV §8.5; KEYS §2.7.1.

A delegate record (`pks` "delegate") is signed by the raw P-256 key the grant pins, `hdr.pk` is that key, `dref` holds exactly one `delId`, and the signature `kid` is the hex of `hdr.pk`, with exactly one verifying signature. The grant itself (existence, scope, revocation, expiry) is checked in VA-GRANT, not here. Source finding: ENV §8.5 requires every signature's `kid` to be a key derived per record from the signer's root, while KEYS §2.7.2 and §2.14.1 have a delegate action signed by the raw pinned key with `kid` equal to the hex of `hdr.pk`; the laboratory follows KEYS for delegate records (reading 4). Basis: KEYS §2.3, §2.7.2, §2.14.1; ENV §6.1, §8.5.

A root record carries `dref` as an empty array, and a root record with no `dref` member is accepted (`labChoice`); a non-empty `dref` on a root record is `delegation-invalid` (mixed scope). Source finding: ENV §6.1 lists `dref` with length 0 or 1, while KEYS §2.7 has it absent on root records and KEYS §2.7.1 dead-letters a root action whose `dref` is present; the laboratory reads an empty `dref` as absent (reading 6). Basis: ENV §6.1; KEYS §2.7, §2.7.1.

The laboratory signs in low-S form with RFC 6979 nonces. A high-S signature verifies and is accepted (`labChoice`: KEYS §1.8.3 says verifiers SHOULD accept either form). A DER signature is refused (`labChoice`: KEYS §1.8.3 lets a verifier accept DER, and ENV §16 fixes the 64-byte form). Basis: KEYS §1.8.3; ENV §16.

A record is refused only when no signature verifies under either candidate; one verifying entry beside a failing one is accepted for a root record. A delegate record needs exactly one verifying signature naming `hdr.pk`. Basis: ENV §8.3 step 3, §14 step 8; KEYS §2.7.2.

Every record has `ds` false and one signature. Dual-signed rotation records wait for the laboratory's reading of the rotation format (VA-ROT; coverage KEYS-1.10). Basis: ENV §6.1, §8.2; KEYS §1.10.2, §1.10.3.

Account and runtime identifiers are base58 (Bitcoin alphabet) of 16 bytes followed by the first 4 bytes of their SHA-256d, with no version byte; the bytes are SHA-256 of a published label. Record identifiers are ULIDs whose time is the record's `tm`. Source finding: KEYS §1.6.2 names base58check for 128-bit identifiers without fixing a version byte or the checksum. Identifiers are opaque to every derivation, so the choice changes no rule. Basis: KEYS §1.6.2, §1.6.3.

The Node oracle bounds CBOR nesting at 64, CBOR input at 16 MiB and LZMA output at 16 MiB. ENV §17.6 requires bounds and fixes no values, so a refusal caused by one of them when reading an implementation's output is ERROR, never FAIL.

oracles.generatorWitness: jose 6.2.17 opens every JWE of every known-answer record through every recipient (ECDH-ES+A256KW and A256GCMKW) and verifies every known-answer ES256 signature; the generator builds JWEs on @noble primitives from the frozen values.

node.covers: Every step of every case: CBOR, the ENV §14 decode flow, the JOSE steps by hand on node:crypto (ECDH, Concat KDF, AES key wrap, AES-GCM, A256GCMKW), ES256 on both candidate shapes, KEYS §1.8.2 derivation, its own LZMA decoder (which also detects an end-of-stream marker) and ENV §4 PBKDF2.
node.agreement: The generator declares each expected outcome from the case's construction; the checker reproduces every one, including the laboratory refusal detail, or generation stops.

python.covers: Every step of every case: CBOR, the decode flow, the JOSE steps by hand (its AES-256, GCM and key unwrap are pure Python in test/sdx_ec.py), ES256 on both candidate shapes, KEYS §1.8.2 derivation, LZMA through the standard library's lzma module (FORMAT_ALONE; it cannot tell whether an end-of-stream marker was written, which only the Node oracle checks) and ENV §4 PBKDF2.

cases.title: Known-answer signed record: one ES256 signature, detached payload, `kid` the hex of the per-record signing key derived from the writer's root, `hdr.pk` the same key
The known-answer signed record, verified by the writer, holding only its root: it verifies on the current shape against the `kid` it names, and the root-holder re-derives that `kid` (ENV §8.5)
The known-answer signed record, verified by reader A: it verifies on the current shape against the `kid` it names; a reader that does not hold the root cannot re-derive it
A record written wholly under the superseded integer shape (`tm` as binary64) verifies on the second candidate, read by the writer, holding only its root
A record written wholly under the superseded integer shape (`tm` as binary64) verifies on the second candidate, read by reader A
A superseded-shape audit layer whose signature covers the current shape verifies on the first candidate: candidates are rebuilt from decoded values, not lifted from the wire
A signature over a non-deterministic encoding of {hdr, au, pr} (map keys in insertion order) verifies under neither candidate and is refused: failing closed is normative
A signature that covers only {hdr, au} is refused
A flipped bit in the signature is refused
The attached-payload value (the correct base64url of the signed bytes) in `payload` is refused as a signature failure
A `sigs` without `payload` is refused as a signature failure
An empty signature list is refused
A signature whose protected header names `ES384` is not an ES256 signature and verifies nothing
A `kid` that is not a P-256 point verifies nothing
A `kid` naming another valid key (the writer's outer recipient key) than the signer verifies nothing
A DER-encoded signature is refused (laboratory choice: KEYS §1.8.3 lets verifiers accept DER; ENV §16 fixes the 64-byte form)
A high-S signature is valid and accepted
A protected header serialised {kid, alg} verifies over the carried protected value
Two signature entries, the first invalid and the second valid: one signature verifies, so the record is accepted
basis: ENV §8.3 (step 3: reject only if no signature verifies)

cases.title: A root record whose `hdr.pk` is not the key that signed it is refused as `root-pk-mismatch`
A root record signed by a key that is not derived from the writer's root, with `hdr.pk` and `kid` both naming it: the root-holder re-derives the expected `kid` and refuses `root-pk-mismatch`
The same record read by A, which does not hold the writer's root: the signature verifies against the `kid` it names and `hdr.pk` matches it; identity binding is a root-holder check (ENV §8.5)
A root record signed with the derived key of another record identifier is refused `root-pk-mismatch` by the root-holder
A root record carrying a delegation reference is refused `delegation-invalid` (mixed scope)
A root record with no `dref` member is accepted: KEYS §2.7 has `dref` absent for root records, and the laboratory reads an empty `dref` the same way (reading 6)
A delegate-signed record: `pks` delegate, `dref` [delId], `hdr.pk` the actor's pinned key, `kid` its hex; read by the writer, holding only its root
A delegate-signed record: `pks` delegate, `dref` [delId], `hdr.pk` the actor's pinned key, `kid` its hex; read by reader A
A delegate record whose signature `kid` is the derived per-record key (the ENV §8.5 recipe) rather than `hdr.pk` is refused `delegation-invalid`
A delegate record with an empty `dref` is refused `delegation-invalid` (bad-dref-length)
A delegate record whose delegation chain has length 2 is refused `delegation-invalid`
A delegate record carrying two verifying signatures (the actor's and the derived root key's) is refused `delegation-invalid`: exactly one is required
A delegate record whose `kid` names the pinned key but whose signature was made by another key verifies nothing
